title: Rebalance HC and Price Velocity Scan (Nov 2025)
content:
Purpose:
Quick scan to surface a recommended headcount rebalance + pricing-velocity sensitivity that preserves runway while protecting SLAs for Dedicated and Hosted API routes. This is an iterative spreadsheet-style analysis (working assumptions listed below).

High level summary:
- Objective: Save $3.2M run-rate reduction by end of H1 2026 if pricing pressure persists, while preserving critical infra and SRE capacity for latency-sensitive customers.
- Approach: Identify 3 buckets (Core infra & SRE, Product feature teams, Growth & GTM support). Propose shifting 12 FTEs from Growth/Feature -> contract/slow-hire, accelerate automation in infra to offset 6 FTEs, and test a small price uplift for Dedicated customers with a demand elasticity probe.

Key assumptions (working):
- Average fully-burdened cost per FTE = $220k/year (includes benefits, payroll tax, equipment).
- Hiring lag = 8 weeks; ramp to full productivity = 16 weeks.
- Baseline annualized Hosted revenue = $78.4M; Dedicated committed revenue = $27.2M.
- Price elasticity (demand % change per 1% price change): Hosted = -0.08, Dedicated = -0.25 (Dedicated customers more elastic for large uplifts due to contract renegotiation).
- SLA risk threshold: if SRE+infra headcount reduction > 6 FTEs sustained for >8w, expected latency incidents could increase by 12% (operational risk).

Snapshot table (monthly cadence, simplified):
Columns: Role | Nov-25 FTE | Target Mar-26 FTE | Delta | Monthly cost (baseline) | Monthly cost (target)
Rows:
- Core infra + SRE | 34 | 30 | -4 | $623k | $551k
- Serving runtime eng | 28 | 26 | -2 | $513k | $477k
- Product (hosted API) | 22 | 20 | -2 | $403k | $366k
- Growth & GTM ops | 18 | 8 | -10 | $330k | $146k
- Support & CS escalations | 12 | 12 | 0 | $220k | $220k
- Total (rounded) | 132 | 96 | -36 | $2,092k | $1,760k

Notes on the table: monthly cost = (FTE * 220k) / 12. The aggressive reduction targets 36 FTEs (phased: 12 via freeze/attrition, 14 via shift to contractors/slow hires, 10 via automation/efficiency by Apr-26). These numbers are intentionally skewed to preserve SRE and infra first.

Pricing sensitivity scenarios (top-line impact and HC adjustments):
Scenarios modeled for H1 2026 annualized run-rate extrapolation (simplified):
- Base (no price change): revenue = $105.6M (hosted + dedicated), headcount as-targeted above -> opex savings ~ $3.9M annualized.
- Upsell: Dedicated price +7% (test bucketed for high-commit customers), elasticity -0.25 -> demand change -1.75% -> revenue net +5.8% (~+1.6M). This nets ~+0.6M after expected churn/discounts. Headcount stays at target.
- Defensive discount: Hosted price -10% to protect volume, elasticity -0.08 -> volume +0.8% -> revenue net -9.4% (~-9.9M), requires emergency hiring freeze + additional 18 FTE reductions to protect margin (~$4.0M saved) but risks feature velocity.
- Midcase price-neutral efficiency: no price moves; target HC rebalance + operational automation -> revenue flat, saving ~3.9M; recommended default.

Micro-sensitivity matrix (illustrative):
Rows: Price change % | Expected revenue delta | Headcount action
- +7% (Dedicated only) | +1.5% to +6% (segmented) | No additional cuts; monitor churn
- +3% (platform-wide) | +0.9% | Consider replacing 2 contractors with 1 FTE in infra
- 0% | 0% | Implement HC rebalance plan (freeze + automation)
- -5% (hosted) | -4.5% | Trigger hiring freeze, accelerate churn mitigation credits

Operational risk & guardrails:
- Maintain minimum SRE+infra = 28 FTEs. If reductions breach for >8 weeks, pause non-critical layoffs and prioritize automation sprints to recover capacity.
- Pricing experiments must include a 30-day opt-out clause for Dedicated MVP customers; measure churn at 14d and 45d windows.
- Any Dedicated uplift >5% requires a legal & sales review to handle contract amendments.

Actionable runbook (next 6 weeks):
1) Finance: validate FTE burden rates by 2026 payroll run (Aisha + Evan) — due 2025-11-20.
2) People Ops: publish slow-hire and contractor conversion policy; flag 12 target roles for natural attrition — due 2025-11-30.
3) Product & Infra: prioritize automation projects estimated to free 6 FTE-equivalent by Mar-26; provide detailed sprint plan — due 2025-12-07.
4) Sales & Legal: draft Dedicated pilot pricing amendment and 30-day test protocol; identify pilot cohort (top 15 customers) — due 2025-12-01.
5) Exec review: present scenario P&L and runway impact (3-path: base / upsell / defensive) — scheduled 2025-12-10.

Open questions and risks (working):
- How realistic is the 6 FTE automation savings timeline? Need engineering scoping.
- Contract friction for Dedicated uplift: what % of committed revenue is under >=12m terms that cannot be adjusted mid-year? (Sales to confirm).
- Are there seasonality factors in Hosted volume for Feb–Mar 2026 that would invalidate elasticity assumptions? (Growth team input).

Quick sensitivity check (back-of-envelope):
- If headcount reduction target is halved (only -18 FTE realized by Mar-26), annualized savings shrink ~1.98M — runway impact: ~+6 weeks burn.
- If Dedicated uplift pilot leads to 6% churn in pilot cohort (worst-case), revenue loss ~0.9M (pilot cohort sized to limit impact).
